questions.model_answer: What I like most is that I don't have to drive in heavy traffic. I can read on the bus, and I don't have to pay for parking downtown.

questions.set_intro: Imagine that a friend calls to ask how people get around in your city. The two of you talk by phone about public transportation.
questions.question: If a friend were visiting your city for a week without a car, would you recommend public transportation? Why or why not?
questions.model_answer: Yes, I would recommend public transportation for a week-long visit. Buses reach the main markets and the riverfront, and a weekly pass costs much less than taking taxis every day. I would tell my friend to avoid the morning rush hour and to check the route map before heading out. With those two simple steps, an unfamiliar city is much easier to get around.

questions.question: When you need to study, do you prefer to study alone or with a group? Explain your choice with reasons and a short example.
questions.model_answer: I prefer to study alone, especially when the material is new. When I am by myself, I can reread a hard sentence without asking other people to wait, and I remember more of what I put into my own words. Last term I tried a study group before a history test, and we spent much of the hour talking about the schedule instead of the chapter. A group is useful later, when I want someone to check whether my answers are clear. For the first pass, though, quiet time with my notes works better. That is why I would still choose to study alone, and I would invite classmates only after I have finished that first careful reading on my own.
